question.problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a force of magnitude $(2x+{x}^{2})\,\text{N}$ acting in the direction of increasing $x.$ Given that $x$ is measured in meters, calculate the work done by the force in moving the particle from $x=0$ to $x=2.$
question.worked_solution:
The work done by a force $F=F(x)$ in moving a particle from $x={x}_{1}$ to $x={x}_{2}$ is given by

$$
W={\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}F(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

When the force and distance are measured in Newtons and meters, respectively, the work done by the force is measured in Joules ($J$).

Substituting the given values into our integral, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}W & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(2x+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[{x}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}({2}^{3})-({0}^{2}+\frac{1}{3}({0}^{3})) \\  & =4+\frac{8}{3}-0 \\  & =\frac{20}{3}\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
